title: Show what you know about body science
learning_goal_display: I can use models and evidence. I can show what I know about skeletons, muscle pairs, nutrition, balance and food.

ta_brief_html:
Full staff brief

Science book routine and adult support

Beside the You do, mark I (independent), S (supported) or C (choice): the level of independence, not the effort.

Give time to start → point to the relevant place → rephrase → offer a small prompt or word bank → reduce to a limited choice. Never straight to telling the answer.

No cold calling; nobody is asked to read difficult text aloud.

Tell the teacher the barrier: reading, vocabulary, processing, regulation, writing or a science misconception. Avoid prompting through every question or dictating the final answer.

E Evidence on the school's evidence app

Lean capture on the school's evidence app (E): 30-second clip, photo, or one-line context note.

Point, sign, repeat after the adult, demonstrate, a clip on the school's evidence app, choice board.

If behind

A pupil who missed last lesson: give the Arrival reminders and today's must-know words, not the missed lesson's work.

Arrival and Starter

Arrival 1: Which protects the brain: skull or stomach? Answer: Skull.

Arrival 2: A muscle gets shorter and pulls. Is that contract or relax? Answer: Contract.

Arrival 3: A dog has a backbone; a worm does not. Which is a vertebrate? Answer: The dog.

Arrival 4: J has 5 g sugar per 100 g; K has 10 g per 100 g. Which has less? Answer: J.

Starter: Which part pulls to bend the arm: a bone or a muscle?

You do routes

Independent is the preferred route: the task is completed in the book without answer-giving support. Supported uses a small nearby prompt; Choice uses limited options and a short scientific sentence, label or reason.

Choice: For each evidence card, choose between its two clues: skull protects brain/stomach; biceps contracts/relaxes to bend; carbohydrate gives energy/hearing; grass/rabbit starts the chain. Choose the better model foot spacing from the counts. In your book, label one answer per card and complete: Food helps muscles because ____.

Practical method and access

Photograph the practical at the planned point, upload it to the school's evidence app with this code, and stick a copy in the book.

Lesson code: SCI-BUILD-A1-W08-P2

Method strip · stick in your book
  1. Set out the four prepared evidence cards; do not lift or pull another person’s arm.
  2. Choose one card and locate the named structure, label or unit with the adult. STOP AND CHECK with the adult before continuing.
  3. Use the diagrams or your own comfortable movement to inspect the clue; pointing is an equivalent route.
  4. Record what the clue shows and one link between the body, food or movement ideas.

Only the apparatus for the current stage goes on the table. If safe participation is not possible, watch the teacher demonstration and record an observation and one conclusion in your book.

After the practical, record what you observed and one conclusion linked to today’s learning goal. Add a method or diagram only where it is part of the learning.

Planned photograph point: after the observation is recorded and before the pupil writes the conclusion. Model evidence is identified as model evidence; it never proves independent practical completion.

P17 · SLT planning and evaluation

Lesson code: SCI-BUILD-A1-W08-P2

SoW reference: BUILD scheme of work, Autumn 1 review of weeks 1–7

Exact SoW outcome: I can use models and evidence to show what I know about skeletons, muscle pairs, nutrition, balance and food sources.

Evidence (scheme of work): Pearson Entry Level Science 8939 (E1→E3 intro); AQA UAS science units. Supported : working-scientifically observation & results tables. S: end-of-unit assessment + Entry Level / UAS evidence.

Evidence in this lesson: Book responses to four strands, one because connection, the model or number used, prompt level, and the exit; individual responses stay private.

Evidence location: Independent work and exit answers in books under the strip; any spoken or pointed answer is recorded as the pupil’s exact response with support level.

Label evidence on the school's evidence app with this code: SCI-BUILD-A1-W08-P2. For spoken, practical or photographic evidence, record the same code with the evidence.

Stage plan and staff moves

Stage and minutesTaskStaff move

Which is a vertebrate? J has 5 g sugar per 100 g; K has 10 g per 100 g. Which has less?Support the selected route privately. Four short clues; no public marks.
Starter · 3 minWhich part pulls to bend the arm: a bone or a muscle?Do not read answers until pupils have responded. Use the misconception for discussion.
I do · bones and a muscle pair · 5 minWhat pulls the forearm when the elbow bends?Alternate bend and straighten. Name the contracting muscle and trace which bone moves. Skeleton reference is available in a disclosure.
We do · match the bone jobs · 5 minMatch each clue to support, protection or movement. Then explain the animal clue.Keep every original bone-job clue and the backbone contrast; answers stay gated in question activity.
I do · food and model evidence · 4 minWhich spacing stayed up more often?These model results are labelled invented; they are evidence interpretation, not a pupil practical completion. Read nutrient table aloud.
We do · organise a food chain · 4 minDraw the arrows. Explain what each arrow means.Build the chain with the order cards, then get all answers at once. Use private RAG after the book response.
Independent · use the evidence · 1 minWhich clue backs your answer?The four evidence cards are referenced; use the diagrams on earlier stages and the organiser. No new practical.
Independent · connect the science · 10 minWhich model or number supports your answer?Read five route questions individually; privately note RAG against success criteria. Supports and pictures are valid, no public score.
Review and improve · 1 minChoose one answer to improve after a quiet prompt. Add a clue or a because reason; mark //.One adult gives VF; one gathers private RAG. Ask for one self-edit or a spoken next step.
Exit ticket · show your clue · 3 minShow what you understand. Write or draw under today’s work; an adult can write your words.Read this private closure with the support used in mind. Use it to set Autumn 2 starts and routes.

Planned adaptations

Cognition and learning: Arrival and independent: show one of the four evidence cards at a time; point to the deciding clue before moving on; fade the prompt once the pupil continues.

Communication and interaction: We do and check: read one option aloud, allow silent planning and accept point, sign, drawing or exact scribing; wait before revealing.

SEMH: Arrival and review: use a predictable first–then cue, a private check-in and an agreed pause/re-entry. Give one quiet next step with no public scores.

Sensory and physical: I do and independent: use projected diagrams or large adult-prepared cards; no forced handling, balancing, lifting or pulling a person’s arm.

EAL: Starter and model: rehearse skeleton, contract, nutrient and food chain with the diagram; permit first-language planning and a because stem. EAL is not SEN.

EEF strategy: explicit instruction; cognitive and metacognitive strategies; scaffolding; flexible grouping; technology used where it improves access.

Staff: confirm the planned adaptations actually used and record any changes below.

If behind

Must teach core: Preserve one individual response on bones, muscle pairs, food/nutrition and food-chain direction, plus one because link and the exit evidence.

Shorten or merge: Shorten repeated group card rehearsal after a secure check; use the reference cards without handling. Keep the independent responses and private review.

Next lesson: Autumn 2 W01 Discover: reduce, reuse and recycle. Start with the science strand and prompt level identified by the private RAG rule below.

Dependency: Pass on checked understanding and unresolved errors for the next starter. A group product does not replace an individual response. Record any coverage change.

Staff evaluation

  • Date taught: record privately.
  • Delivered as planned: Yes / Partly / No.
  • Criteria met: All / Most / Some; record each criterion and support used.
  • Adaptations made and why: record what changed access or understanding.
  • Change from the SoW and coverage impact: record any shortening, merging or remaining dependency.
  • Evidence banked: record the lesson code on the school's evidence app.

P18 · Individual target opportunities

Cognition and learning: Independent · connect the science: choose the deciding clue on one evidence card and connect two ideas using because; record attention, sequencing or independence and prompt level.

Communication and interaction: We do · match the bone jobs: give a clue in the agreed response mode, then receive a partner’s reason; record an individual communication or turn-taking target.

SEMH: Arrival: use the agreed start and pause/re-entry plan; review: accept one private VF and try one precise NS. Record the pupil’s own regulation or engagement target.

Sensory and physical: I do · bones and a muscle pair: track the contracting muscle with an agreed pointing or access method; do not require movement or handling. Record target-related access and independence.

EAL: Starter · what bends the arm?: use contract and relax in an explanation with a diagram and because stem; allow first-language planning and rehearsal. EAL is not SEN.

Capture E against the pupil's own IEDP target on the school's evidence app; the IEDP carries their EHCP-linked and Boxall targets, so one record serves every plan. Follow the pupil's IBSP where it differs from these routines.

Staff AfL and next teaching moves

Feedback and marking · this lesson

Staff copy — not for pupil books. Codes live in books, never on pupil slides or printouts.

Lead with VF. Practical and exit tasks carry no written-comment expectation (Curriculum Policy 2026/27 §14.3: written marking where it adds value, typically Launch GCSE and Functional Skills writing).

Codes

VFVerbal feedback given here
WSWorked with support
IIndependent
NS + …Next step one specific thing
EEvidence captured on the school's evidence app
RResponded loop closed (Audience has happened)
//Self-edit point
?Read this back to me

Curriculum Policy 2026/27 §14.3 summary: VF WS I NS E R (six codes; NS “next step”, E “evidence on the school's evidence app”, R “responded to feedback”). The Feedback Policy, the code source, adds // and ? and expands NS to one specific thing and R to loop closed.

Margin edits: in the same colour, on the same page.

The R gate

  • Voice — point, sign, verbal response, demonstration, re-attempt, edit or authorised short clip.
  • Audience — an adult genuinely receives the response.
  • R only when both happened.

NS + … prompts, one per route

  • Supported — You have written that the bone pushes the muscle. Show me which one pulls.
  • Independent — You have named a job the skeleton does. Add the clue that shows it.
  • Aspire — Check your food-chain arrow. Say what it is pointing at and why.

Read the cause, not the child

CauseWhat you seeNext teaching move
Securenames the job and gives the clue that establishes itask for a second clue from a different body system
Mixednames the job but the clue belongs to another jobmodel one job and its clue, then re-ask
Misconceptionsays the bone pushes the muscle, or reverses the arrowdemonstrate the pair pulling, then re-draw one arrow
Access barriercan point to it on the model but cannot write ittake the answer by pointing and scribe it
Method or datathe evidence card does not carry the clue neededswap in a card that does before judging the answer

Involvement moment — We do · match the evidence

Pupil voice is invited here and can be recorded as VF. Voice is point, sign, verbal response, demonstration, re-attempt, edit or authorised short clip — pointing, signing, demonstrating and re-attempting all count, not only speaking.

Arrival line

“Last lesson your evidence showed __, so today we’re starting with __.”

Use the last lesson’s evidence only if it is available. Otherwise begin from today’s four arrival responses.

Preparation and teaching

Use the organiser and the four supplied evidence cards as a desk-based route; all answers go in books. If using a card arm, an adult prepares the joint and checks any split pin. No food is eaten. Use models for balance rather than asking pupils to demonstrate physical balance. We will look, work as a group, then use the evidence on our own.

Real-world link

Practical, everyday link (Build): reading the label on a lunch or a snack to spot protein, carbohydrate and calcium; lifting a school bag to feel the biceps pull while the triceps lets go.

Carry the check into the next science lesson

Read the existing subject work and exit. Classify the cause of uncertainty, then teach one next move at the next planned science lesson. Begin with a truthful spoken inheritance sentence. A secure response can transfer to a fresh example. Mixed or misconception evidence calls for one precise re-model. Access and method problems call for an adjusted route before rechecking meaning. A missed close remains closed; there is no extra completion task.

Private RAG rule for every success criterion

Green: shown independently (I). Amber: shown with support (WS), or partly. Red: not yet shown. Scores are never read out. Record the criterion, response, support and next teaching move privately. Change access before judging science understanding.

First lesson back staff routine

Before the lesson, scan the books for five minutes.

Ask the cover teacher and TAs what was taught.

Check the roll against the books.

Existing NS+ is history. Begin fresh feedback.

After the check, one read, once, to shape Autumn 2.

Optional model reference · preserved retrieval and opening questions
Arrival task

BUILD · SCIENCE · AUTUMN 1 · WEEK 8 · USE

Optional retrieval reference

In your book: Glue in today’s strip; date it. Number four short answers.

Choose your route and think about bones, moving, animals and food. Write or draw answers in your book.

Choose a route. Think first, then check the answers together.

1. Bones and jobs

Which job does the skull do: protect the brain or digest food?

Help with this question

Think about what is inside your head.

Answer: The skull protects the brain.

2. A muscle moves

A muscle gets shorter and pulls. Is that contract or relax?

Help with this question

You can show the idea with your hand or point to a word.

Answer: Contract.

3. Animal evidence

A dog has an internal backbone. A worm does not. Which is a vertebrate?

Help with this question

Vertebrate means an animal with a backbone.

Answer: The dog is a vertebrate.

4. Sugar evidence

J has 5 g sugar per 100 g. K has 10 g per 100 g. Which has less sugar?

Help with this question

Compare the same amount of food.

Answer: J: 5 g sugar per 100 g.

1. Skeleton job

Name one job of a skeleton and a bone that helps do it.

Help with this question

Think about holding up, protecting or moving.

Answer: For example: the skull protects the brain. Ribs protect the heart and lungs. Bones hold the body up and work with muscles at joints.

2. A muscle pair

When the biceps contracts to bend an arm, what does its partner do?

Help with this question

Muscles pull. Think about what the triceps needs to allow.

Answer: The triceps relaxes and gets longer in this simple model.

3. Classification

Say what vertebrate means. Use the word backbone.

Help with this question

Use a body part on the inside as your evidence.

Answer: A vertebrate is an animal with a backbone inside.

4. Compare with support

J: 5 g sugar per 100 g. K: 10 g per 100 g. Write one comparison and back it up.

Help with this question

Keep the number, the unit and the per 100 g together.

Answer: J has less sugar per 100 g than K: 5 g compared with 10 g.

1. Bones with two jobs

How can bones protect us and also help us move?

Help with this question

Give two named examples, or describe two jobs.

Answer: The skull or ribs protect organs. Muscles pull bones at joints, so we move.

2. Pulling back

Why does a joint need a pair of muscles to move both ways?

Help with this question

Explain how the move can go back the other way.

Answer: Each muscle pulls when it contracts. The partner pulls the other way. Muscles do not push the bone back.

3. Food source

What does the arrow mean in grass → rabbit?

Help with this question

Follow the food and its stored energy.

Answer: Food and energy pass from the grass to the rabbit when the rabbit eats the grass.

4. Limits of evidence

J has less sugar per 100 g than K. Does this show everything about a healthy diet? Explain.

Help with this question

One nutrient is not the whole diet.

Answer: No. We also need the other nutrients, how much is eaten and the whole diet.
